messages:
marie: Heads-up: during the nightly perf run on prod-dedicated pool I observed steady GPU memory growth over ~2h. Dumped profiler snapshots and a small repro. attaching gist: https://redwood-gists/abc123 :eyes:

jason: Can you paste the top of the gpu_profiler snapshot? even a short excerpt might show alloc size distribution.

marie: pasted snippet:
```
# snapshot 1743509123
Allocations by size:
  64B x 1.2M
  4KB x 320k
  1MB x 12k
Total reserved > used by ~1.1GB
KV cache lookups normal (hit rate unchanged)
```

samir: That smells like fragmentation. Did we change workspace sizing or allocator flags in canary this week?

marie: We bumped ALLOC_WORKSPACE_MB 128->256 on Tue canary. Also enabled buffer_reuse=true in runtime config to reduce cold overhead.

nate: Quick suspicion: small-churn allocations from batching+kvcache merging. Try running the repro with drained KV and smaller workspace; I usually run:
`python tools/repro_mem_growth.py --iters 200 --batch 4 --kv 256`

marie: ran that repro, growth reproduced locally too. Here's the reduced repro I used:
```
# repro_mem_growth.py (snippet)
for i in range(args.iters):
  out = model.generate(input_ids, do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=1)
  cache = model.kv_cache.detach()  # intentionally keeping refs to reproduce
  if i % 50 == 0:
    print(i, torch.cuda.memory_reserved())
```

jason: Oof — keeping refs to the KV cache will pin buffers even if the allocator frees them. Try `cache = None`, `gc.collect()` after use. Note: `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` only releases unused cached CUDA memory to the allocator; it doesn't magically defrag.

marie: removed the persistent refs and re-ran. Growth stops, but fragmentation remains: reserved vs used gap ~600MB. So not a leak (no ref retention) but bad fragmentation for this churn pattern :disappointed: 

samir: Next test plan: enable allocator compaction and lower workspace to force different binning behavior. Set `ALLOC_COMPACT=1` and `ALLOC_WORKSPACE_MB=96`; also try `RUNTIME_BUFFER_POOL=true` (allow reuse across requests). If reserved drops we know allocator heuristics are the issue.

marie: quick experiment: ALLOC_COMPACT=1 + ALLOC_WORKSPACE_MB=96 -> peak reserved dropped from ~1.1GB to ~300MB, runtime perf stable on a short run. Promising. Will run full 8h load test tomorrow and upload traces.

nate: Also add kernel-selection traces to the run. Small alloc churn can flip kernels (small/large matmul variants) and hide perf regressions. Collect `kernel-picker.log` + `batching-stats` for that test.

marie: created PERF-1423 with snapshots, repro, and initial traces. tagging @samir @nate. Thanks everyone :heart:
